extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: Labeled subsets of the tiny images dataset: CIFAR-10 contains 10 object classes with 6000 images each, and CIFAR-100 contains 100 classes with 600 images each.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The labeled subsets were created by paying students to filter noisy labels from the Tiny Images dataset. Labelers reviewed images retrieved by class search terms and their WordNet hyponyms, rejected images not belonging to the assigned class, and the authors personally verified every submitted label. Duplicate images were then removed and the data split into training and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source was the Tiny Images dataset, originally collected from the web by searching for every non-abstract English noun in WordNet using search engines including Google, Flickr, and AltaVista, keeping roughly the first 3000 results per search term.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm using a liberal rejection threshold to capture perfect duplicates as well as re-saved JPEGs and similar near-duplicates. The dataset was then split into training and test sets, with 5000 randomly selected training images per class.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the underlying Tiny Images source, perfect duplicates and images with excessively large white regions were removed. For modeling, images were downscaled to 32x32; some experiments whitened the data and deleted the 1000 least-significant principal components.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Students were paid to label a subset by filtering out mislabeled images from noisy search-term labels. Each labeler was assigned a class and examined images found with that class term and its WordNet hyponyms. Labelers rejected images not in class according to criteria including likely category name, photo-realism, single prominent object, and clear identity despite occlusion or unusual viewpoint. Every submitted label was personally verified by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset relied on noisy search-term labels as initial labels, then human filtering and author verification to improve reliability. Duplicate removal was also applied after labeling.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The original Tiny Images labels are extremely unreliable because they come from web image search terms.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The underlying Tiny Images dataset has no reliable class labels, making it hard to use for object recognition experiments. The original search-term labels are extremely unreliable.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The Tiny Images dataset is used for unsupervised training of deep generative models, while CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 provide reliable labels for object recognition experiments. The paper uses CIFAR-10 for training and testing classifiers, with a training/test split of 5000 training images per class.
